findings.evidence: "Your ASCII mockups should be production-ready blueprints" and "Focus on clarity, consistency, and practical applicability" are generic quality assurances. The body is almost entirely familiar UX guidance and task activation rather than specialist knowledge.
findings.fix: Remove the self-praise and compress generic quality assurances. Replace them with concrete layout heuristics, such as keeping comparison fields aligned across repeated records while reserving stacked layouts for independently scanned items.

findings.evidence: "For each mockup, briefly explain" the design approach and strengths requests retrospective rationale, but the ordered workflow supplies no decision framework for developing meaningfully different layouts.
findings.fix: Before drawing, rank the primary user tasks, identify required content that must remain invariant across alternatives, and assign each variant a distinct trade-off. Evaluate the resulting layouts against those tasks before writing their rationales.

findings.evidence: "Be properly formatted and easy to read" is a generic positive instruction; the body contains no concrete anti-patterns, NEVER rules, or rendering gotchas with reasons.
findings.fix: Add an ASCII-specific Gotchas section: never align columns with tabs because viewer tab stops differ; never substitute emoji or Unicode box-drawing characters in ASCII-only output because encoding and display-width assumptions can fail; explain how these mistakes damage the mockup.

findings.evidence: The unquoted description contains "Examples: <example>Context: User" and additional colon-space sequences. These invalidate a YAML plain scalar. A plugin agent can fall back to its filename, but its routing description and other frontmatter settings are not reliably loaded.
findings.fix:
Replace the frontmatter with valid YAML, using a folded scalar to satisfy YAML's colon-space constraint:
---
name: ascii-ui-mockup-generator
description: >-
  Create ASCII UI wireframes with distinct layout alternatives, design rationales,
  and a component handoff. Use when users want to explore dashboard, form,
  navigation, or screen layouts before implementation, including requests to
  sketch how an interface could look. Not for implementing UI code or producing
  high-fidelity visual designs.
model: sonnet
color: green
---

findings.evidence: "Create 3-5 distinct ASCII mockup variations" is unconditional, including for a requested single layout or a small revision to an already selected design.
findings.fix: Default to three structurally distinct alternatives for exploratory requests, but honor an explicit option count and produce only the requested revision when refining an existing mockup.

findings.evidence: "Be ready to iterate based on user feedback" leaves the task open-ended. Numbered ASCII mockups and rationales specify an output format, but no sentence states when the task is done.
findings.fix: Add: "The initial task is done when the numbered ASCII mockups, their rationales, and a selection question have been delivered. A refinement task is done when the requested changes and any requested implementation handoff have been delivered."

findings.evidence: "Demonstrate responsive considerations when relevant" leaves the narrow-viewport branch unresolved: there is no target character width, overflow fallback, or validation-and-repair step for layouts whose content does not fit.
findings.fix: Establish target character widths before drawing and state assumptions when widths are unspecified. When content exceeds a target width, stack fields or explicitly mark horizontal overflow rather than breaking borders. Before delivery, check required components and row alignment, repair violations, and repeat the check.
